issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds the scalar |\bar u| by \sqrt{L_v M_max}\|u-\bar u\|_v^h, but then uses this as a bound on \|\bar u\|_v^h, which equals \sqrt{L_v}|\bar u|; as written the chain only gives (1+L_v\sqrt{M_max})^2. Moreover \|M\|_v^{h,2}\le L_v M_max is not valid in general (only \le L_v M_max^2, or \le M_max via the normalization). The discrete Poincaré step is also off by a factor 1/\Delta v relative to the final summed inequality. The stated \gamma_h does hold, but only via a corrected argument (\|M\|^2\le M_max from normalization, or orthogonality \|u\|^2=\|u-\bar u\|^2+\|\bar u\|^2).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use \|M\|_v^{h,2}\le M_max (from \langle M,1\rangle=1), then \|\bar u\|_v^h=\sqrt{L_v}|\bar u|\le\sqrt{L_v M_max}\|u-\bar u\|_v^h, and fix the \Delta v bookkeeping in the Poincaré step.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the coercivity constant is not valid as written; the constant itself survives after correcting the intermediate steps, so Theorem thm:main_AP is not invalidated.
issues.title: Coercivity proof: intermediate inequalities do not yield the stated constant as written
issues.why_classification: Local routine correction; the stated constant and all downstream results are preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: With the defined symmetric diffusion stencils, \beta\otimes T^{(\alpha)}+\beta^{-1}\otimes T^{(1/\alpha)} is not equal to \mathcal L_h from eq:fp_discrete_separable: the \beta-part of the true stencil is (\alpha_{q+1/2}f_{q+1}-\alpha_{q-1/2}f_q)/\Delta v^2 and the \beta^{-1}-part is (\alpha_{q-1/2}^{-1}f_{q-1}-\alpha_{q+1/2}^{-1}f_q)/\Delta v^2. Also, for the stencils as defined, the induced norm bound would be 4\alpha_max/\Delta v^2, not 2\alpha_max/\Delta v^2. The stated \kappa_h is correct only for the (unstated) true two-term operators.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine T^{(\alpha)}w_q=(\alpha_{q+1/2}w_{q+1}-\alpha_{q-1/2}w_q)/\Delta v^2 and T^{(1/\alpha)}w_q=(\alpha_{q-1/2}^{-1}w_{q-1}-\alpha_{q+1/2}^{-1}w_q)/\Delta v^2, for which the 2\alpha_max/\Delta v^2 and 2/(\alpha_min\Delta v^2) bounds hold.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Proposition prop:fluctuation_bound rests on a false operator identity; the final constant \kappa_h remains valid once the velocity operators are defined consistently with eq:fp_discrete_separable.
issues.title: Fluctuation bound proof uses a tensor decomposition that does not match the stencil
issues.why_classification: Local redefinition fixes the proof with the same constant; nothing downstream changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs M_max^{n+1}\ge M_{p,q}^{n+1} at grid nodes (to bound \|\rho M\| and \|g\|), but the Assumption defines it as the maximum of the geometric-mean half-grid values \sqrt{M_{p,q}M_{p,q+1}}, which is strictly smaller than the nodal maximum for a Gaussian on a grid. The inequalities as written are therefore not justified with the stated constant. (The coercivity proposition likewise uses M_max, M_min without definition.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define M_max^{n+1}=\max_{p,q}M_{p,q}^{n+1} (nodal maximum) and M_min analogously; all inequalities then hold.
issues.overall_effect: The constants in eq:residual_bound and eq:distance_bound are slightly understated; the structure of the theorem is unaffected.
issues.title: M_max^{n+1} defined over half-grid values but used to bound nodal Maxwellian values
issues.why_classification: A one-line definitional correction preserves the theorem and its bounds.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Although Theorem \ref{thm:main_AP} only proves AP property up to the spatial fluctuation  $\mathcal{O}(\kappa_h)$
We provided a theoretical analysis for the first-order low-rank scheme, proving an asymptotic–preserving property in the case of small spatial field fluctuations.

issues.failure_explanation: Abstract and conclusion claim an AP property is proved for small field fluctuation. Theorem thm:main_AP only bounds the distance to the local Maxwellian by \varepsilon\|G\| plus a term proportional to \kappa_h that does not vanish as \varepsilon\to0 for any nonzero fluctuation; it also says nothing about consistency with the limiting drift system eq:macro_drift. Genuine AP is established only in the case \kappa_h=0 (spatially constant field), and the whole result is conditional on the formal assumption \|G^{n+1}\|=O(1) and on Assumption asm:small_fluct with \gamma_h\propto M_min.

failure_location.quote: For the first-order scheme, we prove an asymptotic-preserving (AP) property when the field fluctuation is small.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rephrase abstract/introduction/conclusion to state that a bound on the distance to local equilibrium of order \varepsilon plus the field-fluctuation constant \kappa_h is proved, with exact AP only for spatially constant fields.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised theoretical guarantee (AP for small fluctuation) is stronger than what is proved; the formal theorem and remarks themselves are accurate.
issues.title: Prose overstates the AP result: theorem gives an epsilon-independent O(kappa_h) residual, not an AP limit
issues.why_classification: Only the wording of the summary claims needs weakening; no formal result is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
with spatially localized density and background charge
\[
  \rho^0(x)=0.3+\exp\!\Big(-\frac{(x-0.3)^2}{0.01}\Big),\qquad
  \eta(x)=0.3+\exp\!\Big(-\frac{(x-0.6)^2}{0.01}\Big),
$\eta(x)$ is a given background charge satisfying the global neutrality condition \(\int_{\Omega_x}(\rho(x,0)-\eta(x))\,\dx=0\)

issues.failure_explanation: Integrating f^0 in v gives \rho^0(x)(1+\sqrt{T_cold})\approx1.07\rho^0(x), so \rho^0 is not the density of f^0 as stated, and \int(\rho(x,0)-\eta)dx\neq0 since \int\rho^0=\int\eta. The periodic Poisson problem eq:Poisson then has no solution as written, so the test problem is ill-posed unless the beam is renormalized or the mean is subtracted.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Normalize the two-component profile (e.g., divide by 1+\sqrt{T_cold}) or state that the Poisson right-hand side is mean-corrected.
issues.overall_effect: The bump-on-tail experiment is not reproducible from the stated data without an unstated normalization; no theoretical result depends on it.
issues.title: Bump-on-tail initial data: rho^0 is not the density of f^0 and neutrality fails
issues.why_classification: A local renormalization of the test data restores well-posedness; no claim beyond the experiment description is affected.
